messages:
Maya Chen: Quick q — proposing an eval split protocol for the reranker bring-up on the new retriever+rerank stack. Want to avoid session leakage and make the test reflect production drift. Opinions?
Sam Patel: Agree on leakage concern. Are we sticking with per-user session dedup or moving to time-based holdout?
Maya Chen: I sketched two options:
```
# A: time-based
train: <= 2026-01-01
val: 2026-01-02 .. 2026-02-01
test: > 2026-02-01
# B: stratified dedup
# dedup queries/docs across splits by fuzzy token Jaccard > 0.8
```
I prefer A to simulate drift, but B helps remove near-duplicate paraphrase leakage. Also thinking of reserving a small "head queries" bucket for targeted AB checks.
Jon Reyes: Time-based is better for prod-like behavior. But even with time splits, paraphrases can leak. Add fuzzy dedup post-split (Jaccard or sim threshold) to flag near-duplicate queries and docs.
Lina Gomez: For metrics: NDCG@10 and MRR@10 as primary, but report per-intent buckets (navigational vs informational) + pos-normalized NDCG to surface preference flips.
Priya Kaur: Note from quantization runs: last week's 4-bit reranker had ~0.6% absolute NDCG@10 drop on MS MARCO. However top-1 flips concentrated on a small set of queries. We'll need per-query deltas and significance.
eval-bot: eval-bot: run 1772104402 finished. baseline:v2 candidate:llama-re-rank-q4 dataset:msmarco-time-split. Summary: NDCG@10 delta = -0.62% ; MRR@10 delta = -0.47% ; artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood/test-1772104402 (upload contains per-query CSV and ranklists).
Maya Chen: :thinking_face: thanks. Can someone pull per-query hist and a top-k confusion matrix? I want to see which intents drive the degradation.
Sam Patel: Uploading artifacts now. Also flag on formatting — we currently do passage concatenation up to 512 tokens and lowercase everything. That may remove product codes / case signals.
Jon Reyes: Let's run two formatting variants in the same eval: (1) keep-original-case + punctuation, (2) lowercased + strip-punc. Split results by query length buckets (short/medium/long).
Lina Gomez: Add Recall@k and Pairwise-Swap accuracy (percentage of pairwise orderings where candidate > baseline) — helps quantify swaps even when NDCG delta small.
Priya Kaur: For stats: use bootstrap (20k samples) to get 95% CI for NDCG delta. Also compute per-query p-values and apply Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple tests.
Sam Patel: I'll kick off formatting variants + quantization ablations (fp16, q4, q4+sym) on the temporal split. ETA ~2 hours.
Maya Chen: :thumbsup: if we see head queries degrade more than tail, consider preserving some weights in fp16 (e.g., output head / final linear) or using mixed-precision for top-k logits.
Jon Reyes: Agreed. Also capture eval-config in metadata: split seeds, dedup thresholds, tokenizer version, model compile flags, prompt templates used.
eval-bot: eval-bot: job 1772104701 started (formatting-variants + q-ablation).
Sam Patel: Noted — I will save per-intent NDCG, per-query delta hist, and top-1 flip lists. cc @Priya Kaur so she can run significance tests when done. :eyes:
Priya Kaur: On it.
Maya Chen: Thanks team. Let's reconvene tomorrow EOD for rollout decision. Quick process note: for any candidate that beats baseline by >0.2% NDCG, add a small human eval sample (n=200 top-5 judgments) before greenlight.
Sam Patel: Will add human-sample job to the pipeline if candidate passes automated thresholds.
Jon Reyes: Also let's log tokenization diffs per-query (token counts before/after formatting) — sometimes truncation causes missing context that explains drops.
Maya Chen: Good point. Adding that to the run checklist.
Lina Gomez: TL;DR: time-based split + post-split fuzzy dedup, report NDCG@10/MRR@10 + Recall@k + pairwise swap, run formatting variants, bootstrap CIs, human-check on +0.2% wins.
Maya Chen: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
